title: Cavity Tuning of the CDW--Superconductivity Interplay in a Kagome Metal
authors: Lan-Ting Shi, I-Te Lu, Xin Wang, Dongbin Shin, Lede Xian, Angel Rubio
abstract: Kagome metals host competing electronic orders, including charge-density-wave (CDW) order and superconductivity, shaped by intertwined lattice, electronic-correlation, and kagome-geometric effects. Here, using quantum electrodynamical density functional theory, we identify an equilibrium cavity route for reshaping this balance in the kagome metal CsV$_3$Sb$_5$. An out-of-plane polarized single-mode cavity selectively softens CDW-related phonons, counteracting pressure-induced hardening and extending the CDW instability toward higher pressures. In the high-pressure regime where the CDW instability is otherwise suppressed, cavity coupling redistributes Eliashberg spectral weight toward lower frequencies, enhances the total electron--phonon coupling (EPC), and increases the EPC-based Allen--Dynes estimate of $T_c$. This response originates from a charge-density redistribution induced by the out-of-plane photon mode, which modifies lattice restoring forces and drives the phonon and EPC renormalization. These results establish cavity quantum electrodynamics as a viable equilibrium route for tuning intertwined charge order, lattice dynamics, and superconductivity in kagome materials.
summary: The authors used QEDFT calculations on CsV3Sb5 to show that coupling the material to an optical cavity acts as a powerful tuning mechanism for competing electronic orders. By selectively softening CDW-related phonons, the cavity enhances electron-phonon coupling and boosts the superconducting critical temperature, establishing cavity quantum electrodynamics as a viable control route in strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The study investigates how an external cavity field can tune the competition between Charge-Density-Wave (CDW) order and superconductivity in a Kagome metal.
main_result: Cavity coupling selectively softens CDW-related phonons, extending the instability to higher pressures and enhancing electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda$), thereby increasing the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$).
method: The research employs quantum electrodynamical density functional theory (QEDFT) to model cavity light-matter coupling effects on lattice dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Kagome metal CsV3Sb5. The theoretical framework involves modeling the interaction between electronic structure, lattice vibrations (phonons), and an out-of-plane polarized single-mode optical cavity field.
key_observables: CDW soft phonon frequencies, total electron–phonon coupling ($	ext{EPC}$) strength ($\lambda$), Allen–Dynes estimate of $T_c$, and charge density redistribution ($\Deltaho$).
important_parameters: Hydrostatic pressure (tuning CDW instability) and dimensionless cavity coupling amplitude ($A_0$) are the primary tuning parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis tracks harmonic lattice instabilities, not the full finite-temperature anharmonic CDW transition line. The method relies on first-principles QEDFT calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how cavity coupling selectively softens specific phonon modes (counteracting pressure hardening) and maps the resulting charge redistribution ($\Deltaho$) which drives the enhancement of low-frequency EPC.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a theoretical framework using QEDFT to model cavity interaction, demonstrating that this interaction acts as an equilibrium tuning knob. It shows selective phonon softening first, followed by calculating the resultant enhancement in $	ext{EPC}$ and $T_c$ due to charge redistribution.
why_interesting: This work directly applies advanced quantum electrodynamics (QED) techniques to condensed matter physics, treating the cavity field as a controllable external perturbation that modifies fundamental material properties like lattice dynamics and superconductivity. This bridges AMO concepts into solid-state materials science.

FIG. 2. Competing effects of pressure and cavity cou- pling on phonons in CsV3Sb5. (a) Phonon dispersions at different hydrostatic pressures, showing progressive hard- ening of low-frequency modes and suppression of the CDW instability. (b) Phonon dispersions at 3 GPa under different cavity-field couplings A0, compared with the outside cavity case. The cavity selectively softens low-energy phonons, coun- teracting the pressure-induced stabilization of the lattice.
